faq.q: What does “life’s teachers are everywhere” mean?
faq.a: It means every person, experience, and challenge can teach you something if you are open to the lesson. Learning continues long after school ends.

faq.q: Who said “When the student is ready, the teacher will appear”?
faq.a: The saying is widely shared but its origin is uncertain. It is often misattributed to the Buddha or Lao Tzu.

faq.q: What are examples of unexpected teachers in life?
faq.a: Children, strangers, animals, nature, difficult people, hard seasons, and your own mistakes can all be powerful teachers.

faq.q: How can I learn more from everyday experiences?
faq.a: Get curious instead of defensive, slow down enough to notice, look for repeating patterns, and keep a simple weekly lesson log.

faq.q: How do I thank a teacher who made a difference?
faq.a: Send a short, specific message about what they taught you and how it stayed with you. Teachers rarely hear how the story turned out.

faq.q: Do painful experiences always have a lesson?
faq.a: Many do, but the meaning often comes later. Give grief and pain room to be felt before trying to find the silver lining.
